weakness: The pipeline grasped the mouse from above with nothing to do when that was blocked: with four light, taller objects 1.5-2 cm from its sides and ends, every grasp approach was refused and the run ended with the mouse untouched.
how_found: Questioned A2 (nothing stands next to the mouse) because a mouse on a real desk sits between a keyboard, a phone and papers; the frozen pipeline scored 0.0.
why_missed: The phase-1 scenes had a bare desk, so 'grasp' meant one API call with no look at what surrounds the object.
fix: Not recovered within 6 repairs (v1: 0.0, 0.3, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4; base stayed 0.9-1.0; the phase-1 pipeline is kept and the last attempt is in unsolved/v1_pipeline.py). Tried: (1) move every small object within 5 cm of the mouse to a free table spot before the grasp -- 0.0, because the top grasps of those objects put the fingertips into the table (grasp point 3 cm below a 6 cm top, fingertips 3.6 cm below the grasp point); (2) that fixed, and only the objects on the sides the fingers close on -- 0.3: the mouse grasp was still refused, the end objects block it too; (3) all sides again, no second-arm retry -- 0.7; (4) a second try for an object that slips off on the lift (one finger has to go down a 1.5 cm gap beside the mouse) and clearing again before a retry -- 0.6, now over the 120 s budget; (5) drop each object from 4 cm instead of lowering it, no move home in between -- 0.5; (6) slide an object that cannot be lifted lengthwise past the mouse -- 0.4. Clearing four objects costs 50-80 s of the 120 s, and the runs that failed ran out of time or had one object that could be neither lifted nor slid.
general_rule: When the object to grasp is hemmed in, first work out which neighbours actually block the grasp you will use and how long clearing each one costs, and move only those, cheapest first, keeping enough of the time budget for the task itself; a gap narrower than a finger cannot be used for a grasp.

weakness: The pipeline chose one arm, from the side the mouse lies on, and used it for the whole task. With the pad on the other side of the desk (0.68 m away, across the robot's body) the place step found no path on any seed and the mouse was never released on the pad.
how_found: Questioned A1 (the arm on the mouse's side can also reach the pad) because the phase-1 pad always lay in the middle of the desk, where both arms reach; on a real desk the pad can be anywhere. The frozen pipeline scored 0.0.
why_missed: In every phase-1 scene the pad was at the robot's middle, so 'the arm that can pick it up' and 'the arm that can put it down' were always the same arm and the choice was never tested.
fix: Choose the placing arm from where the pad is. When it is not the picking arm, the picking arm sets the mouse down on the table in the middle (reached by both arms), goes home, and the other arm picks it up there and puts it on the pad (base 1.0, v1 unchanged, v2 1.0; the relay adds about 16 s).
general_rule: Choose the arm for each reach from where that target is, not once for the whole task; when no single arm reaches both the start and the goal, hand the object over through a spot both arms reach.

weakness: The pipeline grasped the mouse only through the API's annotated grasp points. With the mouse lying upside down every one of those points faced the table, so each grasp target lay below the table top and was refused; no grasp was ever attempted.
how_found: Questioned A6 (the mouse lies flat and right side up) because things on a desk get knocked over, and a mouse on its back is a common sight; the frozen pipeline scored 0.0.
why_missed: Every phase-1 mouse lay right side up and the annotated grasp always worked, so there was no reason to write a second way to take hold of it.
fix: When the annotated grasps fail, grasp the mouse's detected box from above, closing across its narrowest horizontal side, with the fingertips just above the table (base 1.0, v2 1.0, v3 0.9 after 1 repair; the miss was a 2.2 cm placement against the 2 cm tolerance).
general_rule: Do not depend on one source of grasp points: when an object's pose makes its stored grasps unusable (they point into its support), fall back to a grasp computed from its measured shape in the pose it is actually in.

weakness: The pipeline carried the mouse to the pad centre and lowered it without looking at what stood there. With a mug-sized object left on the pad, every way down was blocked (or pushed into the mug) and the mouse ended back on the table beside the pad.
how_found: Questioned A5 (the space above the pad is free): a cup left standing on the mouse pad is an everyday sight. The frozen pipeline scored 0.0.
why_missed: The pad was always bare, and the only object the pipeline ever looked at was the one it carried.
fix: (1) Before picking the mouse up, while the hands are free, move every small object standing on or at the edge of the pad to a free table spot away from the pad, the mouse and the way between them -- 0.3: the grasp of the 10 cm object was refused because the descent started 5 cm above a grasp point 3 cm below its top, so the fingertips began inside it. (2) Start a grasp from above with the fingertips above the object's top -- base 1.0, v2 1.0, v3 0.9, v4 0.9.
general_rule: Before carrying something to where it must go, check that place for anything standing on it and clear it while the hands are still free; and start every approach from above with the fingertips clear of the object's top, not at a fixed distance above the grasp point.

weakness: The pipeline only ever put the mouse down with the hand pointing straight down. With the pad at the back of the desk, where the wall shelf's lower board overhangs the pad's back edge 15 cm up, every straight-down hand over the pad had its wrist under the board, so no put-down pose was reachable and the mouse never reached the pad.
how_found: Questioned A10 (the pad can be reached from straight above) after screening five candidates against the round-4 pipeline: walls between mouse and pad, the pad at the desk's front edge, a slippery desk and a 1.5x mouse did not break it cleanly (1.0, 0.9, 0.9, 0.4 with the big model probably too wide to grasp); the pad against the shelf did (0.0).
why_missed: Every earlier pad lay in open space, and a hand pointing straight down was always the easiest put-down, so the hand's own size above the goal was never considered.
fix: (1) When no straight-down hand reaches over the pad, also try the hand tilted 20-31 deg about its closing axis so that the wrist leans towards the robot, away from what overhangs the goal -- v5 0.7, the misses were 2.2-2.5 cm placements: the tilted mouse moved as it fell flat. (2) Lower a tilted mouse 1.2 cm past first contact, so that it lies flat on the pad before it is let go -- base 0.9, v2 1.0, v3 0.8, v4 0.8, v5 0.8.
general_rule: Check the space the hand and wrist need above a goal, not only the goal itself; when something overhangs it, tilt the hand so the wrist stays clear, and press a tilted object flat onto the surface before letting go so that it does not shift as it settles.

weakness: The pipeline only ever reached down at the mouse. With the mouse pushed half under a monitor riser (a fixed board 8 cm above the desk over its back half), every grasp from above had the wrist under the board and was refused, and the API's own grasp sometimes closed on the board instead.
how_found: Questioned A2 from above rather than from the side (the space over the mouse is free): a mouse pushed under a riser or a shelf is common on a real desk. The frozen pipeline scored 0.0.
why_missed: Every earlier mouse lay in the open, and the only obstacles so far stood next to things, not over them.
fix: Five repairs (v7 0.1, 0.1, 0.4 -- the same code re-measured gave 0.8 --, 0.6, 0.8). (1) Grasp the exposed end and draw the mouse out -- the mouse slipped out of a hand holding it 3 cm from its end. (2) Let go once it is out and grasp it again at its centre, and check the grip before aligning over the pad. (3) Draw it out until its centre is 11 cm past the board's edge, so the hand fits. (4) Look for an overhang first, and try end grasps with the wrist leaning away from the board -- on the smaller mice only 4-5 cm stick out, less than the fingers need beside the exposed end, so the fingers met the board. (5) Come in level from the open end along the mouse's length, the fingers on its two long sides passing under the board, close at its centre, slide it out and lift: base 1.0, v2 1.0, v3 0.8, v4 0.8, v5 0.9, v7 0.8.
general_rule: When part of an object is under something, do not reach down at it: come in level from the open side, low enough to pass under the overhang, take it by its middle and slide it out into the open before lifting.
